observation.summary: VoicePacketCortex.close_session() rejects nonterminal output but does not reject or explicitly fence active tool ownership. After emitting SESSION_CLOSE it sets is_open=false and clears _active_tools silently. By contrast barge-in explicitly moves active tools into _cancelled_tools and restart/reentry explicitly fences restored active tools stale.
observation.candidate_risk: A session may produce a terminal VoiceOutcome while a TOOL_USE ownership record is still active, then erase that ownership without an explicit cancellation/fence event. A later external tool completion is necessarily rejected because the session is closed, but the packet-cortex event history no longer contains a causal tool-cancellation/fence transition explaining the ownership terminalization.
observation.scope: packet-cortex tool ownership / session-close causal atomicity only

high_information_discriminator.precondition: Create one open VoicePacketCortex; emit TOOL_USE with a unique tool_ref; keep all output terminal/no output so close is otherwise legal.
high_information_discriminator.action: Call close_session() before TOOL_RESULT for the active tool_ref, then inspect return/exception, event log, active/cancelled ownership state, exported checkpoint, and behavior of a synthetic late TOOL_RESULT attempt.
high_information_discriminator.candidate_failure_condition: close_session succeeds while the active tool disappears from ownership without an explicit cancellation/fence event or preserved tombstone sufficient to prove why later completion is stale/cancelled.
acceptable_repair_shapes: fail closed: refuse SESSION_CLOSE while any active tool ownership remains
explicit terminalization: atomically fence/cancel every active tool before SESSION_CLOSE and preserve causal tombstones/events
high_information_discriminator.required_regression: A close attempt with active TOOL_USE cannot silently erase tool ownership; restart/export and late-result behavior must remain deterministic and auditable.
